clinical_features.symptoms:
symptoms prior to arrival 
•
Document specific features of TCA OD: 
Sedation/coma/seizures 
Metabolic acidosis 
Broad complex tachydysrhythmias, hypotension 
Anticholinergic syndrome 
ECG changes 
•
Further investigations: FBC, U&E, LFT, Paracetamol/Salicylate level, urine tox 
screen 
 
ECG FEATURES 
•
Na channel blocking agent 
•
Sinus tachycardia 
•
Prolonged PR interval 
•
Interventricular conduction delay – QRS > 100 ms 
QRS > 100ms predictive of seizures 
QRS > 160ms predictive of ventricular arrhythmias 
•
Prolonged QT interval 
•
RBBB 
•
Right axis deviation of the terminal QRS 
Terminal R wave > 3mm in aVR (tall R wave) 
R/S ratio > 0.7 in aVR 
TRICYCLIC ANTIDEPRESSANT OVERDOSE 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
Significant overdose > 10 mg/kg 
 
SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT 
FURTHER MANAGEMENT CONSIDERATIONS 
• 
Hypertonic saline 3% 100ml boluses if Sodabic unavailable 
• 
3RD line treatment: 
• 
IV Sodium bicarbonate 1- 2 mmol/kg (1 - 2 ml/kg 8.4% or 2 - 4 ml/kg 4.2%) 
■ 
Indications: pH < 7.1, QRS > 100ms, arrhythmias, seizures, hypotension 
■ 
Repeat every 5 minutes until BP improves and QRS complexes narrow 
■ 
If arrhythmias occur, cardioversion is unlikely to be successful, continue Sodabic boluses until 
rhythm normalizes 
■ 
If seizures occur, Sodabic is the 1st line treatment 
• 
Intubate early for airway protection and hyperventilation – BEWARE WORSENING ACIDOSIS 
• 
Hyperventilate to maintain pH at 7.5 – 7.55 
• 
Administer 1g/kg activated charcoal via NGT ONLY once airway is protected (even if presentation > 1 
hour after ingestion). Consider MDAC in severe cases 
• 
Benzodiazepines can be used for seizures, AVOID ANTI-EPILEPTIC DRUGS 
• 
Fluid bolus 20ml/kg crystalloid, consider inotropes if still hypotensive 
THE MAINSTAY OF TREATMENT IS SODIUM BICARBONATE AND HYPERVENTILATION 
Lignocaine 1.5 mg/kg IV for arrhythmias once pH >7.5 
• 
Consider Magnesium Sulphate if significant QT prolongation 
• 
Consider Intralipid in consultation with GIT/ICU 
• 
Consider ECMO in refract
